content.text: I have enough to conclude. No redline is needed — the document affirmatively protects our freedom to source elsewhere.

input.quote: Client is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink hereunder, so long as such
input.rationale:
The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Client, so it meets the preferred position. Section 2(a) (p0022/p0024) goes further than mere silence: the licence is expressly "non-exclusive" and Client "is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink," subject only to a non-infringement and confidentiality carve-out that does not restrict sourcing. A full-text sweep for "exclusive", "sole", requirements-contract and "shall not procure from any third party" formulations found no covenant binding Client: the only other hits are the non-exclusive licence of Credit Data to TrueLink (p0054), an exclusive-forum clause (p0094), and a reference to a separate Non-Competition Agreement that limits TrueLink's use of Credit Data (i.e., runs in our favour and is not an exclusivity obligation on us).

Noted but not flagged: §3(i) (p0042) provides that "Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface." This is a narrow tie-in scoped to transactions Client voluntarily routes through TrueLink's Interface, not an all-requirements or exclusive-dealing covenant — Client remains free under §2(a) not to use the Interface at all and to obtain credit reports elsewhere for any other loan. It therefore does not create exclusivity of the kind this rule targets and does not warrant a redline; we would simply resist any future attempt to broaden it beyond Interface-routed transactions.</rationale>
